title_original: Which films are out in front in the foreign-language film races? Plus Ampas’s Meredith Shea on new Oscar rules - The Screen Podcast
excerpt_original: Meredith Shea discusses the new festival-winning pathway for international films to enter the race.

blocks.text: On this week’s episode of The Screen Podcast, we delve into the international feature race on both sides of the Atlantic, and hear from Academy exec Meredith Shea.

First, host Wendy Mitchell is joined by awards and box office editor Charles Gant to break down the international films vying for attention at the Oscars and the Baftas, and the crucial differences between the two.
“You’ve got a whole bunch of [films in the Bafta race] that are the exact same films that are competing at Oscars, and there are 18 of those,” Gant explains

“And then there are 26 other films that are not going to be eligible for the international feature Oscar, but they are being distributed in the UK, they’re coming out in time, they’re not in English language or not primarily in the English language, and therefore they are eligible.”

Then, Americas editor Jeremy Kay chats to Meredith Shea, Ampas chief membership, impact, and industry officer, about the growing international Academy membership and recent changes to the Oscar rules – including the new festival-winning pathway for international films to enter the race.

“We have to make sure that our members are able to watch the number of films and we want to ensure that we’re doing due diligence with the film festivals that are submitting films to us,” Shea said on the possibility of expanding the number of eligible film festivals.

”So having these six inaugural film festivals that are sending films our way was definitely intentional to make sure that we are reflecting the current state of the film industry, but at the same time, we’re pacing ourselves with any rule changes.”
